gap: No result ChatGPT got says that on UGREEN's Nexode 20,000 mAh 100W and 130W banks only the USB-C1 port offers the 15V profile. ChargerLAB measured the Steam Deck triggering that 15V PD profile. USB-C2 on these banks stops at 12V⎓2.5A (30W), so the Deck has to go into C1.
standout_why: I compared against itechguides (cited in the 11-13 chat) and gamingonbatteries.com/best-power-bank-steam-deck (cited 11-10). itechguides only tells readers to 'check the output rating of the specific port' and lists no voltage profiles. gamingonbatteries says the Deck charges at '5V, 9V, 15V, or 20V depending on load' but never says which port to use on a multi-port bank. Neither gives a per-port 15V table for any pick. Neither says the second USB-C on UGREEN's 100W/130W 20K banks lacks 15V. I did not open vgkami.com, which was cited on 11-13.
decides: This confirms the UGREEN Nexode 20,000 mAh 100W, ChatGPT's top pick in both 11-13 chats, but only if the Deck goes into USB-C1. The same rule applies to our listed Nexode 20,000 mAh 130W, whose USB-C2 is 30W max. It also favors the Anker Laptop Power Bank 25K (A1695) for sharing: every USB-C port and built-in cable on it lists 15V⎓3A, so the Deck isn't tied to one port. The Anker 737 (A1289) has 15V⎓3A on both USB-C ports, but Anker's US store shows it sold out, so it should not be a lead pick there.

findings.label: PD voltage the Steam Deck negotiates and its measured input
findings.value: Triggers the 15V PDO; about 39W input from Valve's own 45W adapter
findings.source_title: Exploring the Charging Detail of Your Steam Deck - ChargerLAB Compatibility 100
findings.note: ChargerLAB measured this with a POWER-Z KM002C (article dated 2023-07-18; Deck model not stated). Of the power banks ChargerLAB tested, about half delivered around 35W and the rest 15–25W. None of 80 chargers matched the stock adapter's 39W.

findings.label: Valve's charging spec (LCD)
findings.value: PD3.0 Type C power supply, 45W; 40Whr battery
findings.note: Valve's page gives the wattage and PD version but no voltage/current profile.

findings.label: Valve's charging spec (OLED)
findings.value: 45W power supply (2.5 m cable); 50Whr battery; 20% to 80% in as little as 45 min
findings.note: Charging time is Valve's claim using its own adapter.

findings.label: Which USB-C port has the 15V profile
findings.value: USB-C1: 5V⎓3A/9V⎓3A/12V⎓3A/15V⎓3A/20V⎓5A (PD3.0, PPS). USB-C2: 5V⎓3A/9V⎓3A/12V⎓2.5A only (no 15V). Price $79.99 at UGREEN US
findings.note: Taken from the spec table on UGREEN's US store page, read through the Shopify store tool. USB-C2 max = 12V × 2.5A = 30W. The 'Total Output' row lists 15V⎓3A, a single 45W 15V budget.
